hints: The force $T$ pulls at $35^\circ$ above the slope. Resolve perpendicular to the plane to express the normal reaction in terms of $T$: $R + T\sin 35^\circ = mg\cos 28^\circ$.
For the least value of $T$, the particle is on the point of slipping down the plane, so limiting friction $F = \mu R = 0.2R$ acts UP the plane.
For the greatest value of $T$, the particle is on the point of slipping up the plane, so limiting friction $F = \mu R = 0.2R$ acts DOWN the plane.
Set up the equilibrium equation along the slope for each case and solve for $T_{\min}$ and $T_{\max}$.
walkthrough:
Resolve forces perpendicular to the inclined plane in equilibrium:
$$R + T\sin 35^\circ = 0.8g\cos 28^\circ$$
$$R = 8\cos 28^\circ - T\sin 35^\circ$$

Case 1 (Least $T$): Particle on the point of slipping DOWN the slope. Limiting friction $F = 0.2R$ acts UP the slope:
$$T\cos 35^\circ + F = 0.8g\sin 28^\circ$$
$$T\cos 35^\circ + 0.2(8\cos 28^\circ - T\sin 35^\circ) = 8\sin 28^\circ$$
$$T(\cos 35^\circ - 0.2\sin 35^\circ) = 8\sin 28^\circ - 1.6\cos 28^\circ$$
$$T(0.819152 - 0.114715) = 3.75586 - 1.41272$$
$$0.704437 T = 2.34314 \implies T_{\min} \approx 3.33\text{ N}$$

Case 2 (Greatest $T$): Particle on the point of slipping UP the slope. Limiting friction $F = 0.2R$ acts DOWN the slope:
$$T\cos 35^\circ - F = 0.8g\sin 28^\circ$$
$$T\cos 35^\circ - 0.2(8\cos 28^\circ - T\sin 35^\circ) = 8\sin 28^\circ$$
$$T(\cos 35^\circ + 0.2\sin 35^\circ) = 8\sin 28^\circ + 1.6\cos 28^\circ$$
$$T(0.819152 + 0.114715) = 3.75586 + 1.41272$$
$$0.933867 T = 5.16858 \implies T_{\max} \approx 5.53\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough: Let us identify the forces acting on the particle of mass $m = 0.8\text{ kg}$ on the rough incline of angle $28^\circ$:
2. Normal contact force $R$ perpendicular to the plane upwards.
3. Tension $T$ acting at an angle of $35^\circ$ above the slope.
4. Friction force $F$ along the slope, where at the limits of equilibrium $F = \mu R = 0.2R$.

Step 1: Resolve perpendicular to the plane. The tension $T$ has an upward component $T\sin 35^\circ$ perpendicular to the slope:
$$R + T\sin 35^\circ = mg\cos 28^\circ$$
$$R = 8\cos 28^\circ - T\sin 35^\circ$$

Step 2: Find the least possible value of $T$. If $T$ is minimal, the particle is on the verge of sliding down the plane. Therefore, friction opposes this impending downward motion and acts UP the plane:
$$T\cos 35^\circ + F = mg\sin 28^\circ$$
$$T\cos 35^\circ + 0.2R = 8\sin 28^\circ$$

Step 3: Find the greatest possible value of $T$. If $T$ is maximal, the particle is on the verge of sliding up the plane. Therefore, friction acts DOWN the plane:
$$T\cos 35^\circ - F = mg\sin 28^\circ$$
$$T\cos 35^\circ - 0.2(8\cos 28^\circ - T\sin 35^\circ) = 8\sin 28^\circ$$
$$T(\cos 35^\circ + 0.2\sin 35^\circ) = 8\sin 28^\circ + 1.6\cos 28^\circ$$
Thus, the least value of $T$ is $3.33\text{ N}$ and the greatest value is $5.53\text{ N}$.
